scope: Eight industry/foundation award records; sponsor eligibility, funding, nomination, cycle and URL review.

before.name: Apple Scholars in AI/ML PhD Fellowship
before.whoFor: PhD students in machine learning, vision, NLP, and on-device AI (University nominated)
before.deadline: September 8, 2026 (Annual invited university nomination; internal deadlines July/August)
before.amount: Full tuition and fees for 2 years + annual living stipend + mentorship from Apple AI/ML researchers + internship opportunities
before.summary: Recognizes graduate students pursuing research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, offering funding, mentorship, and opportunities to intern with Apple's ML research teams.
eligibility: Full-time PhD student at participating university in final 2–3 years of study
Nominated by eligible academic institution
Specialization in machine learning, computer vision, speech, robotics, or privacy

after.name: Apple Scholars in AI/ML PhD Fellowship
after.whoFor: University-nominated PhD researchers in artificial intelligence and machine learning
after.deadline: University nomination; current nomination deadline not publicly announced — contact your institution
after.amount: Research funding, Apple researcher mentorship and internship opportunities; current public announcement does not specify tuition/stipend amounts
after.summary: Supports university-nominated AI/ML doctoral researchers through funding, mentorship and internship opportunities. The latest public cohort announcement is for 2026; a public 2027 nomination timetable has not been confirmed.
eligibility: PhD research in artificial intelligence and machine learning
University nomination; current cycle eligibility details and internal selection deadlines must be confirmed with the institution

updates.remaining: Current invitation-only nomination deadline, full funding terms and remaining-years eligibility are not in the public sponsor announcement; do not reuse campus/prior-year dates.

before.name: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program
before.whoFor: PhD students in GPU computing, computer architecture, graphics, AI, and systems
before.deadline: October 30, 2026, including recommendation letters (applications open September 30, 2026; shifted later in the year from the prior mid-September cycle)
before.amount: Up to $60,000 per award + required paid summer internship at an eligible NVIDIA office before the award year
before.summary: Supports doctoral students who are advancing GPU computing, computer graphics, parallel computing architecture, and accelerated machine learning systems.
eligibility: Must have completed at least one year of PhD studies by the time of application
Major in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related discipline
Research actively leveraging GPUs / accelerated computing

after.name: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program
after.whoFor: Full-time PhD researchers in computing, engineering or related fields whose work is relevant to NVIDIA
after.deadline: October 30, 2026, including recommendation letters (2027–2028 award; applications opened September 30, 2026)
after.amount: Up to $60,000 for stipend, tuition and mandatory fees, paid through the university + required in-person summer internship before the award year
after.summary: Supports doctoral students who are advancing GPU computing, computer graphics, parallel computing architecture, and accelerated machine learning systems.
eligibility: Normally at least one year of PhD study completed before applying; exceptional research-experienced applicants may be considered
Full-time PhD enrollment throughout the nine-month 2027–2028 award year; no graduation before its end
Available for an in-person summer internship at an eligible NVIDIA research office before the award year; international PhD students may apply
University administers the award; full-time NVIDIA employees and immediate family members are ineligible
Two or three recommendation letters, including the thesis advisor; all due with the application

before.name: NVIDIA Academic Hardware Grant Program
before.whoFor: Faculty and principal investigators needing GPU acceleration for research and teaching
before.amount: High-end workstation GPUs (RTX 6000 Ada), enterprise server cards, or NVIDIA DGX Cloud credits
before.summary: Grants cutting-edge NVIDIA GPUs and compute resources to university faculty researchers exploring breakthrough applications in AI, graphics, robotics, and computational science.
eligibility: Faculty member or research director at accredited university
Proposals must demonstrate how NVIDIA accelerated computing will advance the research

after.name: NVIDIA Academic Grant Program
after.whoFor: Full-time faculty at accredited institutions awarding PhD research degrees; applications currently unavailable
after.deadline: Not accepting new applications; reopening date not announced
after.amount: Cloud computing, hardware and/or software resources; allocations depend on the applicable call for proposals
after.summary: Provides NVIDIA computing resources to support academic research. The sponsor currently states that it is not accepting new applications; no quarterly reopening schedule is confirmed.
eligibility: Full-time faculty at an accredited academic institution awarding research degrees to PhD students
Research must meet the applicable call and proposal requirements; new applications are currently unavailable

updates.remaining: Resource-specific CFP documents and any future reopening timetable require rechecking when applications resume.

before.name: Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering
before.whoFor: Faculty members in first 3 years of tenure-track appointment (Invited university nomination)
before.deadline: March 15 (Institutional nomination); April 20 at 5:00 PM PT (Full proposal; Annual)
before.amount: $875,000 over 5 years of flexible, unrestricted research funding
before.summary: Provides early-career scientists and engineers with flexible, visionary funding to take risks, explore unproven ideas, and establish creative frontiers across computing and natural sciences.
eligibility: Faculty member in first three years of tenure-track appointment
Invited research universities in the US may each nominate two candidates per year

after.name: Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering
after.whoFor: Faculty within their first three faculty-career years at 50 invited US institutions (university president nominated)
after.deadline: March 15, 2026 (institutional nomination); April 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT (application and letters; Annual, latest published cycle closed)
after.amount: $875,000 over five years; each $175,000 annual payment includes $17,500 for university administration and $157,500 for the fellow’s research
after.summary: Provides early-career scientists and engineers with flexible, visionary funding to take risks, explore unproven ideas, and establish creative frontiers across computing and natural sciences.
eligibility: Faculty at one of 50 invited institutions, eligible to lead natural/physical sciences or engineering research, including computer science
For the 2026 call, initial faculty appointment between May 31, 2023 and May 31, 2026; later cycles require their own published eligibility dates
University president may nominate up to two candidates; application includes department-head and three external recommendation letters
Social-science research is ineligible; clinical research, large national facilities and applied national-security research are outside the program focus

before.name: Simons Investigators in Theoretical Computer Science & Mathematics
before.whoFor: Established theoretical CS and math faculty leaders (Institutional nomination)
before.deadline: Historical (program discontinued in 2023; historically late October / early November)
before.amount: $100,000/yr for 5 years for research + $10,000/yr to PI department + $10,000/yr indirect costs ($600,000 total)
before.summary: Provides stable, long-term unrestricted research support to outstanding scientists, enabling them to undertake foundational theoretical breakthroughs in algorithms, complexity, and quantum computing.
eligibility: Tenured faculty at an institution in the US, Canada, UK, or Europe
Nomination submitted by university president, provost, or dean
Distinguished record in theoretical computer science

after.name: Simons Investigators in Theoretical Computer Science & Mathematics
after.whoFor: Established theoretical CS and math faculty leaders (Institutional nomination)
after.deadline: Historical — Investigator program discontinued; last listed award cohort is 2023
after.amount: Historical terms: $100,000/yr for 5 years for research + $10,000/yr to PI department + $10,000/yr indirect costs ($600,000 total)
after.summary: Discontinued program that supported theoretical scientists with an initial five-year research award, potentially renewable for another five years. No new Investigator nomination call is available.
eligibility: Tenured faculty at an institution in the US, Canada, UK, or Europe
Nomination submitted by university president, provost, or dean
Distinguished record in theoretical computer science

updates.remaining: Archive confirms discontinuation and award duration; historical amount, geographic and nomination terms still need an accessible original solicitation.

before.name: Fannie and John Hertz Foundation Graduate Fellowship
before.whoFor: Graduating seniors & 1st-year PhD students in applied computing and physical sciences
before.deadline: October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT (Annual; reference evaluations due first Monday in November at 6:00 PM PT)
before.amount: Up to $250,000 over 5 years (stipend + full tuition + lifelong fellowship community)
before.summary: The Hertz Fellowship provides 5 years of flexible, unrestricted funding to innovators in applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics, and computing. Hertz Fellows gain lifelong mentoring, peer networking, and total freedom in their PhD research.
eligibility: US Citizens or Permanent Residents
College seniors or first-year PhD students
Pursuing a PhD in applied physical, biological sciences, math, or computer science

after.name: Fannie and John Hertz Foundation Graduate Fellowship
after.whoFor: College seniors, first-year graduate students and gap-year applicants planning an applied-science/engineering PhD; standalone master’s students may qualify
after.deadline: October 30, 2026 (Annual; 2027 fellowship application); four recommender evaluations due November 2, 2026 at 6:00 PM Pacific
after.amount: Up to $250,000 over five years; standard option includes $38,000 per nine months + full tuition equivalent, with $5,000/year for dependent children
after.summary: The Hertz Fellowship provides 5 years of flexible, unrestricted funding to innovators in applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics, and computing. Hertz Fellows gain lifelong mentoring, peer networking, and total freedom in their PhD research.
eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents planning a PhD in applied physical/biological sciences, mathematics or engineering, including computing
Normally college seniors, first-year graduate students or gap-year applicants; standalone master’s students/holders may apply, while later PhD applicants need exceptional justification
Funding requires full-time enrollment at a participating US university; applicants may request that a new institution be added
Four recommender evaluation forms; applicants make a moral commitment to provide their skills to the US in a national emergency

before.name: Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship (QInF)
before.whoFor: Teams of 2 PhD students proposing innovative research in computing and wireless tech
before.deadline: December 1, 2025 at 10:00 AM PST (Annual first Monday of December at 10:00 AM PST)
before.amount: $100,000 fellowship per winning student team ($50,000 per student) + Qualcomm mentor guidance
before.summary: Encourages teams of two PhD students from participating universities in the US, Canada, Europe, and India to formulate joint proposals in mobile computing, wireless communications, edge AI, and semiconductors.
eligibility: Teams of two PhD students enrolled at participating universities
Must submit a joint proposal endorsed by faculty advisors
Proposal in Qualcomm priority research fields

after.name: Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship (QIF) — North America
after.whoFor: Teams of two PhD students at eligible US/Canadian universities; at least one member in EE/CS or a related department
after.deadline: October 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM PST (2027 North America application/abstract); selected teams’ full proposals due December 1, 2026 at 10:00 AM PST
after.amount: $50,000 per winning student ($100,000 per two-student team), paid to university departments for research expenses, plus Qualcomm mentorship
after.summary: North America competition for two-student PhD teams proposing innovative computing and engineering research, with staged abstract, selected-team proposal and finalist presentation rounds. Other regional QIF programs have separate rules and schedules.
eligibility: Both members enrolled in PhD programs for the entire Fall 2027–Spring 2028 academic year at one of the 25 universities named in the North America rules
At least one team member from electrical engineering, computer science or a related department
Initial application includes a one-page abstract, faculty recommendation(s), both CVs and signed rules; selected teams submit a full proposal

before.name: IBM PhD Fellowship Award Program
before.whoFor: PhD students in AI, quantum computing, hybrid cloud, and security (University nominated)
before.deadline: August 30, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET (Annual late summer faculty nomination; historically late October)
before.amount: Up to $40,000 stipend + $20,000 education allowance over 2 academic years + pairing with IBM Research mentor
before.summary: Intensely competitive worldwide program supporting graduate students solving challenging problems in AI, quantum information science, cybersecurity, and open-source infrastructure.
eligibility: Nominated by a faculty member at an accredited university
Must be enrolled full-time in PhD program with at least 2 years remaining
Research matching IBM core interest areas

after.name: IBM PhD Fellowship Award Program
after.whoFor: Faculty-nominated PhD students within two years of graduation; current cycle paused
after.deadline: Paused for the 2026–2027 cycle; no new awards; revised program announcement anticipated in Q1 2027 (application date not announced)
after.amount: Last published terms: $40,000 at US universities; $6,000–$25,000 elsewhere; IBM research mentorship
after.summary: IBM has paused new PhD Fellowship awards for 2026–2027 and anticipates announcing a revised program in Q1 2027. The published prior fellowship covers one academic year, with an optional, encouraged internship.
eligibility: Prior terms: invitation-only nomination by doctoral faculty; students cannot self-nominate
Full-time PhD enrollment for the award year, within two years of estimated graduation at nomination, and no transfer of program
Comparable external fellowship/support during the award period is disallowed (academic scholarships excepted); embargo restrictions and employee exclusions apply
No new 2026–2027 awards; future eligibility must be rechecked when the revised program is announced

sourceConflicts: Packard general timeline mentions April 21 once but its April 20 heading and 2026 guideline agree; used guideline April 20.
Qualcomm 2027 rules contain an old Spring 2026 finalist-event phrase; did not copy it. Timeline tab explicitly names 2026 application/2027 finals.
NVIDIA page retains resource-call text while explicitly stating applications closed; closure notice governs current availability.
